transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-21
Start time: 15:00 PT
Duration: ~46 minutes
Attendees: Maya Chen (Redwood AE), Ravi Patel (Redwood SE), Eleanor Park (NovaEdge Partnerships), Diego Ramos (Cloud Platform), Sanjay Kulkarni (Security)

Auto Summary (auto-generated):
Redwood and NovaEdge sync to align on marketplace listing steps and technical integration. Focus on reference architecture for Private/Dedicated deployments on NovaEdge marketplace, security controls (KMS, SSO, audit logs), packaging options (container vs AMI), and a perf/benchmark plan for initial pilot. Agreed next steps and owners.

Transcript:
[00:00] Maya: hey everyone thanks for joining, uh quick roll call, um we got Maya and Ravi from Redwood, and uh Eleanor, Diego, Sanjay from NovaEdge?
[00:08] Eleanor: yep that's us, thanks Maya.
[00:10] Ravi: hey all, thanks for making time, we'll keep this focused — want to align on marketplace listing requirements and reference arch.
[00:18] Diego: great. quick note, we're aiming to have the listing live in Q3 if the tech checks out, and marketing push in early Q4.
[00:26] Maya: perfect, okay first agenda item: listing metadata and packaging. Eleanor, can you run through the checklist?
[00:33] Eleanor: yeah so NovaEdge needs a listing page, pricing tier info, a reference arch diagram, an install artifact (either container image or an AMI/VM image for private customers), and security/compliance artifacts. we also require a sample terraform module for one-click deploy to our marketplace VPC.
[00:49] Ravi: quick question — for the private option are you expecting us to provide an AMI or is container on the customer's cluster acceptable?
[00:56] Eleanor: both are acceptable, but most enterprise customers prefer an image they can run in the NovaEdge managed VPC or on-prem via VM. containerized is fine for cloud-native buyers.
[01:05] Diego: operationally we need a health-check endpoint, metrics exported to our prometheus stack, and an upgrade path.
[01:13] Ravi: good — Redwood can provide a container image and an AMI; we have a private deployment package that includes a helm chart and an AMI for air-gapped installs. We'll include a health endpoint and Prometheus metrics.
[01:23] Maya: good, and we'll include notes on supported GPU types/instance shapes — we typically recommend A100- or H100-class for dedicated inference and T4/GPU options for smaller configs.
[01:33] Sidenote (transcription error): at one point the call auto-captured 'A 100' as 'a one hundred'
[01:38] Sanjay: security — we need to verify KMS integrations and key custody, and whether Redwood supports customer-managed keys (CMK) or HSM-backed keys. also SSO with SAML and SCIM provisioning for RBAC.
[01:49] Ravi: yes we support CMK via vendor KMS integrations, and we have an HSM option for Private deployments. SAML SSO and SCIM are supported for enterprise accounts; we can map roles to tenant-level RBAC.
[02:02] Diego: for networking — we expect support for private link or internal load balancer (ILB) plus mutual TLS between NovaEdge control plane and the Redwood runtime if we do a managed integration. Any constraints on cert rotation?
[02:12] Ravi: cert rotation is handled by the runtime; mutual TLS is supported, and we can do short-lived certs. we'll document the trust chain and rotation policy.
[02:21] Eleanor: also marketplace requires sample logs/audit events format — our ops folks want to see request IDs, user IDs, and minimal payload hashing for PII concerns.
[02:31] Maya: that's fine; Redwood logs include token-level tracing and request IDs, we can add obfuscated payload hashes to satisfy PII rules.
[02:38] Diego: on the reference arch, we'd like a standard pattern: marketplace control plane -> private VPC peering or transit -> ILB -> Redwood runtime (dedicated pool) -> model storage. want to validate that matches your architecture.
[02:50] Ravi: yes that's the pattern. small nuance: we recommend a smart routing layer that can fallback to hosted instances if dedicated capacity is under pressure — we can switch by model variant or region. for marketplace listing we should call that out as an option.
[03:06] Eleanor: ok call that out. customers ask about failover behavior.
[03:10] Maya: great. next topic: packaging and reference arch deliverables. Ravi, can you run through what you'll provide?
[03:16] Ravi: sure — I'll produce a reference architecture diagram (PNG + editable drawio), an AMI bake doc, helm chart snippets, terraform module example for one-click deploy, and an ops runbook that includes health checks, metrics, and cert rotation steps. target ship date — 2026-08-02.
[03:31] Eleanor: that's perfect.
[03:33] Sanjay: for compliance artifacts we will need your SOC2 report and recent penetration test summary — is that something you can share under NDA?
[03:40] Maya: yes we can share SOC2 docs under the partner NDA. we'll also include a summary of our encryption-at-rest and in-flight architecture and key custody options.
[03:50] Diego: performance/benchmarks — to list on NovaEdge marketplace we need guidance on expected latency at 1k RPS and cost per token approximations for the dedicated offering. we also want to run a joint benchmark on a typical e-commerce chat workload.
[04:03] Ravi: for dedicated inference throughput we'll surface examples by model family and sequence length. we'll propose a pilot benchmark: Redwood runs a set of prompts (we can reuse your sample dataset) against our dedicated pool on an H100-equivalent node and produce latency/throughput tables.
[04:16] Eleanor: timeline for the pilot?
[04:18] Maya: propose we spin up the pilot environment after the reference arch is published — say mid-August if all goes well.
[04:25] Diego: that works. we'll provision a test tenant and share credentials.
[04:28] Ravi: note — there may be slight variance depending on quantization profiles; we'll include recommended quantization/FP configs for cost/latency tradeoffs.
[04:38] Maya: good callout. also include caching and KV cache behavior in the runbook — customers care about prefix caching and token cost.
[04:45] Sanjay: on data residency — some NovaEdge customers require logs to stay in-region; can your logging and analytics be region-scoped?
[04:53] Ravi: yes we can configure analytics retention and where logs are stored; for Private deployments logs can be pushed to customer-managed S3/GCS endpoints.
[05:02] Eleanor: marketing ask — we'll want a short blurb and a hero diagram for the listing page; Maya, you'll lead?
[05:08] Maya: yes I'll put together a 1-page co-marketing brief and sample listing copy. we'll include benefits (predictable latency, cost controls, private deployment option) and a CTA to request a demo or start a pilot.
[05:19] Diego: any blockers we should flag now?
[05:21] Ravi: only dependency is access to a NovaEdge test tenant and permissions to deploy the demo artifacts.
[05:26] Eleanor: we'll create a test tenant and hand over limited credentials to the Redwood SEs.
[05:31] Maya: perfect. ok security follow-up — Sanjay feel free to schedule a dedicated session with Ravi for deeper mutual TLS and KMS detail.
[05:40] Sanjay: will do; can we aim for 2026-08-05?
[05:44] Ravi: works for us.
[05:46] Maya: quick QA: any concerns with listing terms — pricing or SLAs you'd need?
[05:50] Eleanor: we typically require a standard marketplace SLA and a pricing tier mapping. we'll send a sample pricing template; Maya you mentioned you have a template?
[05:58] Maya: yes I'll send our pricing template and suggested default tiers, plus optional enterprise uplift for dedicated capacity.
[06:05] (longer section of technical back-and-forth about TLS configs, small transcription glitches, filler words, etc)
[10:12] Ravi: (explaining runtime) so the Redwood runtime supports continuous batching, KV cache for prompt prefixes, and smart routing across regions. note the KV cache name got transcribed as 'K V cash' sometimes in the automated notes.
[10:25] Diego: ok can you include that in the runbook with expected hit rates and cache sizing guidelines?
[10:31] Ravi: yes will include metrics like cache hit ratio guidance, TTL defaults, and how it impacts latency.
[10:37] Maya: also we'll call out model variants and fallback policies; for marketplace listing we should be explicit how we handle fallback to hosted variants to avoid outages.
[10:46] Eleanor: important for customers.
[10:48] Sanjay: any concerns about customer data in the cache? we need assurance that KV cache not retain PII beyond TTL and that logs are scrubbed.
[10:57] Ravi: caches are configurable; we can provide scrubber hooks and TTL enforcement. we'll include a recommended redaction policy in the ops runbook.
[11:06] Maya: ok last section: timeline recap.
[11:09] (team runs through dates)
[11:11] Maya: recap — Ravi reference arch by 2026-08-02; Eleanor sends marketplace checklist by 2026-07-28; Maya pricing + co-marketing by 2026-07-30; security deep-dive on 2026-08-05; pilot planned mid-August.
[11:28] Eleanor: sounds good, will follow up with calendar invites.
[11:30] Diego: thanks everyone.
[11:32] Maya: thanks, we'll wrap — action items and notes to follow.

End of transcript.
